solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

S048-01.notes: 'Although ... meticulously documented' sets up a contrast, and her own cited letters undercut 'inevitable', so the conclusion is unwarranted. A (exhaustive) is praise, which fits the documentation, not a flawed conclusion. C (derivative) means unoriginal; nothing in the text is about originality. D (understated) would mean she claimed too little, but she claimed too much.

S048-02.notes: Fleas from a lake without midges for decades still grew spines readily, so the ability lasted through those decades. A says the opposite (the ability was lost). B is not supported: the fleas were exposed in the lab, and nothing says midges returned. D makes a reproduction comparison the study did not measure. The cost of spines is only background information.

S048-03.notes: To rule out a citywide weather change you need the control: planted streets cooled while unplanted streets held steady. A gives both trends. B gives only the planted-street drop, with no control, so it cannot rule out weather. C compares only 2023 levels, and the gap could have existed before planting. D gives only the 2018 baseline, which is no evidence of cooling.

S048-04.notes: Two independent clauses, with 'however' sitting inside the second, so a semicolon is needed. A creates a comma splice. B creates a run-on (fused sentence). C: a colon would claim the second clause explains or elaborates the first, but here it contrasts with it, so the semicolon is the conventional choice. Inserted, D reads: 'the early 1600s; recent analysis of its paper, however, suggests...'

S048-05.notes: Maxwell's argument replaces the solid-sheet assumption with separate particles, so 'Instead' fits. A (Similarly) wrongly signals agreement with the earlier view. C (For instance) treats the particle model as an example, which it is not. D (Nonetheless) signals concession, but the conclusion follows from the proof rather than going against it. 'Thus' would arguably be smoother, but it is not offered, and B is clearly best.

S048-06.notes: Only C gives the mechanism (ring widths vary with each year's weather) and the comparison (one winter versus a 150-year range). A and D state the result but give no reason and no comparison with radiocarbon dating. B describes only radiocarbon's imprecision.

S048-07.notes: Her praise is limited: cinematography only, while most of the review is criticism. 'Qualified' means limited by reservations. A (effusive) is the opposite. C (anonymous) has no support in the text. D (premature) brings in timing, which the text never raises.

S048-08.notes: Nematodes stayed just as low without fungi as with them, so the marigold effect does not depend on fungi, which favors the toxic-compound explanation. B is undercut: the fungi did not matter, and no distribution of fungi was measured. C: harm to tomatoes was never measured. D is not tested: no sterilized pots without marigolds were described, and the low numbers track the marigolds.

S048-09.notes: The claim is about differential benefit, which needs the user-minus-nonuser gap in each group: 8 versus 4. A uses a raw gain with no control. B covers only the at-grade group. C shows that both groups benefited, not which benefited more.

S048-10.notes: Vint's design holds television viewing roughly constant and still finds a dialect difference linked to time spent in cities, so television is unlikely to be the cause. A contradicts her claim that broadcast speech is not the cause. C: nothing suggests she disputes the generational change itself. D is unsupported: she does not say television helps people keep dialect features.

S048-11.notes: Putting the slip in the drawer of letters she does not intend to answer suggests she will not follow through on her promise, perhaps from pride over not knowing the book. A: nothing in the text concerns suppliers or money. B: she just wrote the title down and studied it, so she has not forgotten it. D is the opposite, since that drawer holds things she won't respond to.

S048-12.notes: Newton believed lenses could never fix the problem, so he built a mirror telescope as a result: 'Accordingly'. B (Nevertheless) is the trap set up by 'wrongly as it turned out', but building a mirror telescope follows from his belief rather than going against it. C: the mirror telescope is not an example of his conclusion. D: no contrast is being drawn.
